prompt: Two variables point to the same object: 'Dog a = new Dog(); Dog b = a;'. What happens when you call 'a.setName("Rex")'?
choices: Both a.name and b.name reflect 'Rex' because a and b point to the same object
A copy of the Dog is created for b
explanation: Java uses pass-by-reference-value. a and b hold the same reference (memory address). Mutating the object through a also affects the state seen through b.
